text:
Marathon Petroleum has fallen 2.2% today and 13.8% over two weeks as oil prices have retreated and refinery margins have tightened. US crude is trading at $89.53 a barrel, down from levels that would have supported higher refining profits; at the same time, US refineries are running at 95.7% capacity with gasoline and diesel inventories relatively full (215.9 million and 104.9 million barrels respectively), which limits the premium refiners can earn by turning crude into finished products. This combination—lower oil prices paired with high operating rates and ample product supplies—squeezes the spread between what refiners buy crude for and what they sell fuel for.

The broader backdrop hasn't helped. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East (Iranian tanker incidents, Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure) have created uncertainty about regional oil supply, yet haven't pushed prices high enough to offset weak refinery economics. Meanwhile, the recent climate summit's failure to commit to phasing out fossil fuels removes a near-term policy tailwind that might have tightened crude supply, leaving the market focused instead on current oversupply dynamics.
